OpenAI, which has until now rented TPUs, is expanding its cooperation with Google to outright chip purchases—a move that could introduce an alternative to an AI computing market centered on NVIDIA GPUs. Google is also widening external sales by supplying TPUs through Oracle Cloud. Still, OpenAI maintains close ties with NVIDIA, including up to $105 billion in credit support for an Ohio data center. The market is watching Alphabet's third-quarter results, due Oct. 28, for cloud growth and progress in the TPU business. ##### Key Elements OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, is reportedly pursuing a plan to directly purchase Google's in-house artificial intelligence (AI) accelerator, the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU). OpenAI, which has until now rented Google TPUs, is broadening the scope of its cooperation to buying the chips outright. The move is seen as one that could crack the landscape of AI computing infrastructure, which is concentrated on NVIDIA GPUs. According to the IT outlet The Information on Oct. 28 (local time), OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI semiconductors. The specific purchase volume, deal terms and price were not disclosed. Neither Google nor OpenAI commented on the details. The TPU is a semiconductor Google designed in-house, specialized for training and inference of AI models. Unlike graphics processing units (GPUs), which are also used for general-purpose computing, it is built to handle machine-learning tasks efficiently. It is drawing attention as an alternative to NVIDIA products among companies seeking to cut costs. This is not the two companies' first semiconductor cooperation. Since June of last year, OpenAI has rented Google's AI chips for use in its services. Now it is going further, considering direct chip procurement rather than merely borrowing computing power through the cloud. OpenAI recently posted a job listing to hire an engineer to lead work optimizing its most advanced models for Google TPUs—a signal that it intends to deepen integration with Google's chip architecture. Google began selling TPUs directly to some customers this year. Contracts with customers including rival Anthropic are underpinning demand. Anat Ashkenazi, Alphabet's chief financial officer, said some revenue from TPU sales contracts will begin to be recognized late this year, with most reflected in 2027. Google is also widening its TPU supply chain through partnerships with cloud providers. Google and Oracle agreed to offer Google TPUs through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) starting in 2027. It is the first time a major cloud provider other than Google will supply TPUs to customers. Oracle plans to expand TPU supply over several years and to add Google TPUs to its existing NVIDIA, AMD and Intel semiconductors so customers can choose computing devices based on the nature of their workloads. Karan Batta, senior vice president of Oracle OCI, described the deal as a multi-year, multi-gigawatt (GW) partnership rather than an experimental deployment. Beyond NVIDIA, OpenAI is also moving to secure its own chips. It unveiled its first in-house AI chip, co-designed with Broadcom, in June and plans to deploy it by year-end. If it also buys Google TPUs directly, it will have a multi-supplier system running NVIDIA GPUs, its own chips and Google TPUs together. The prevailing analysis, however, is that adopting Google TPUs will not lead to a scaling back of OpenAI's cooperation with NVIDIA. Infra & Chips.content: [English](/en/)[IT](/en/en-it/) # Oracle adds Google TPU, broadens AI chip stack to rival Nvidia 입력 2026.10.28. 15:17 [조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) ![Oracle logo. /Courtesy of Oracle](https://biz.chosun.com/resizer/v2/QPADSFXJRRCL3NNLBCFNM6AMM4.png?auth=2d7d86e3703e7c12deda6090efaf4796c278fe0ff389a1ba244f8a82dd97e8e3&width=616) Oracle logo. /Courtesy of Oracle Oracle will add chips from Google and a startup semiconductor company to its Nvidia-centric cloud AI infrastructure. The idea is to strengthen its market push by letting customers choose from a variety of AI processors within a single cloud. According to Bloomberg and Reuters, Oracle on the 27th (local time) unveiled plans to expand semiconductor supply for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas. Google's tensor processing unit (TPU) will be introduced next year, with supply increasing over several years. It is the first case of a major data center operator other than Google offering TPU services. Oracle will install TPUs in its own facilities and handle power, cooling, and networking. The two companies' collaboration began in databases. After they released a cloud partnership in Jun. 2024, they launched Oracle database services within Google Cloud in four regions across the United States and Europe in Sep. of the same year. Corporations use Oracle databases while using Google Cloud's services. This TPU introduction can be seen as the two companies' collaboration expanding from data management to AI compute infrastructure. The range of choices for AI inference chips will also widen. Cerebras equipment will be deployed starting in the first half of next year, and chips from SambaNova Systems will also be offered. Nvidia maintains an edge in the AI training market, but competition in inference is intensifying among custom chips and startups. It will also expand cooperation with Nvidia. Oracle plans to scale up the latest AI server already offered on OCI, "Vera Rubin NVL72," to the multi-gigawatt (GW) level. The contract amount was not disclosed. Securing funds for the massive investment is a challenge. Oracle did not explain how it will finance the chip additions. Earlier, saying customers' chip expense burdens are rising, it kept its fiscal 2027 capital spending plan at $90 billion to $95 billion. The share price fell 47% from its year-to-date high on Jun. 1 due to the burden of data center investment. ※ This article has been translated by AI. Infra & Chips.content: ![]() ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-light.svg) ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia Faces Fresh Challenge as OpenAI Expands AI Bets ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alphabet.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/openai.svg) OpenAI is reportedly planning to buy artificial intelligence chips from Alphabet's (GOOG) Google, a potentially significant shift as the ChatGPT maker looks to diversify the enormous amount of computing infrastructure needed to train and deploy its models. Final terms of any potential agreement have not yet been determined, according to multiple media reports. OpenAI is already one of the world's largest buyers of Nvidia [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg)NVDA](/symbols/NASDAQ-NVDA/) GPUs, which remain central to both AI model training and inference. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) A deal with Google would therefore be notable because it could give OpenAI another major source of AI computing capacity while reducing its reliance on a single chip supplier. For Google, the implications could be equally important. The company has spent years developing its own AI accelerators to support internal workloads. Selling more of those chips to outside AI developers could turn that investment into a much larger commercial business. The reported talks also highlight how rapidly the AI infrastructure market is evolving. Leading AI companies increasingly need massive quantities of specialized processors, power and data-center capacity, making supply diversification strategically important. That does not necessarily mean Nvidia is being displaced. OpenAI's compute requirements are large enough that the company could continue purchasing substantial quantities of Nvidia GPUs even while adding Google chips to its infrastructure. Instead, the move would suggest that AI developers increasingly want access to multiple hardware platforms rather than depending on one architecture. **Investor Takeaway** I think the biggest potential read-through is for **Google's AI infrastructure ambitions**. If OpenAI becomes a meaningful buyer of Google-designed chips, Alphabet would not simply be competing with OpenAI at the model level. It would also be supplying infrastructure to one of its biggest AI rivals. For Nvidia, the development is worth watching but does not automatically imply lost demand. OpenAI's compute needs continue to expand, and adding another supplier could simply reflect how difficult it is to secure enough capacity. For investors, the key things to watch are **the size of any agreement, which Google chips OpenAI ultimately adopts, deployment timing and whether other major AI developers follow with similar multi-supplier strategies**. The AI chip race may be becoming less about choosing one winner. It is increasingly about securing as much compute as possible from several of them. ## Compare charts ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from GuruFocus](/news-flow/?provider=gurufocus) Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ice.com/fixed-income-data-services).
